hypothesis: Enabling timing-driven net weighting is the baseline-most lever (P-L1) and is currently off; turning it on with the default `adam`-style scheme lets the analytical placer pull critical nets together more strongly, which should reduce many moderate violations (TNS) across all circuits without changing partition/legality.
analysis: The hypothesis held: all three cases are valid and improve, with dWNS and dTNS both positive (e.g., ariane133-ng45 +19.2%/+19.3%, bp-ng45 +12.2%/+15.0%, bp_fe-ng45 +9.4%/+8.7%), consistent with timing-driven net weighting pulling critical nets together and reducing moderate violations without legality issues. Overflow remains nonzero (~103–146), so congestion is a secondary concern. Next step: sweep the net-weighting strength/`adam` parameters and confirm overflow stays bounded, then check whether gains persist at higher utilization.
